statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 11% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for one hour, and in the 19:00 UTC power hour, which reaches WATCH for a second. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Orderly overnight fade off the record close keeps Tail in the low band despite a hawkish rate backdrop
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40, up 250.04 points or 0.82%, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range and at a fresh 52-week and all-time closing high, alongside a second consecutive record Nasdaq Composite close driven by AI enthusiasm around Meta's Muse assistant. Globex NQ now trades 30,991-31,003, roughly 25 to 38 points below the 31,028.50 prior close, inside a narrow 30,992-31,070 overnight band and near its low. That fade off the overnight high is an orderly retracement: no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no holding of a session extreme has been observed since the reopen, which is why Tail stays in the low band. VIX at 14.21 is down 4.44% and settled near its 14.19 session low. The H.15 curve shows the 2-year at 4.76%, the 10-year at 4.96% and the 30-year at 5.29%. WTI at $89.89 and Brent at $98.75 extended a sixth consecutive decline after Iran signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Aramco restarted its East-West pipeline. The genuine tension in this tape is monetary rather than technical: the Fed raised rates last week and Richmond Fed President Barkin said inflation risks outweighed employment risks, with futures pricing further tightening odds, so an elevated curve sits against a record equity high. That conflict, together with narrow semiconductor leadership, raises Stress to 34% in the moderate band while leaving Tail at 11%. Shared Finviz context collected at 00:58 UTC was partial, with futures and calendar sections unavailable; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were used as delayed cross-asset confirmation only and never as live NQ price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a previously published Claude assessment. Tail ranged from 11% to 21%, with the mapped state EA_ON in 21 hours and WATCH in three: the 14:00 UTC cash-open hour and the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block on 22 September. Stress peaked at 46% around the cash open and decayed to 34% by the 01:00 UTC slot as the record close was absorbed, while Confidence held between 84% and 88% throughout. The dominant mode ran as normal through the Asian and European hours, shifted to trend-up after the U.S. open and stayed there into the overnight session. No past assessment has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to hold the low Tail band through the Asian and European sessions, with conditional risk concentrated in the 13:30-15:00 UTC block where the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs coincide, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour after a record close. Two forecast hours reach the WATCH band on the scenario of a continuation leg that denies an early retracement, and both decay quickly once price discovery is orderly, because published Tail is scored down as soon as retracements are observed. Scores return to the overnight baseline once the cash session ends and the 21:00-22:00 UTC futures maintenance break removes the continuous price path. Stress stays inside the moderate band throughout, carried by an elevated yield curve against a record equity high, narrow semiconductor leadership and an unresolved Iran situation rather than by any observed breakdown in mean reversion.
